## Broadcom Stock Locks In Six AI Customers and Charts a Course to $100 Billion

Broadcom Inc. ([AVGO](https://app.tikr.com/stock/about?cid=25016048&tid=555183874&ref=q2enxr)) designs custom AI accelerator chips and infrastructure software, and its Q1 fiscal 2026 results delivered a decisive signal: this is no longer a story about one large customer.

[Total revenue hit a record $19.31 billion in the quarter](https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-inc-announces-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-financial) ended February 2, 2026, up 29.5% year-on-year, with AI semiconductor revenue alone surging 106% to $8.4 billion.

CEO Hock Tan disclosed a sixth AI customer on the [Q1 2026 earnings call](https://app.tikr.com/stock/transcript?cid=25016048&tid=555183874&e=1981933705&ts=3671372&ref=q2enxr), adding OpenAI to a roster that already includes Google, Meta, Anthropic, and two undisclosed hyperscalers, with OpenAI expected to deploy its first-generation custom accelerator at over 1 gigawatt of compute capacity in 2027.

That roster is not a list of transactional buyers.

[Broadcom extended its partnership with Meta](https://investors.broadcom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/broadcom-announces-extended-partnership-meta-deploy-technology) in April to produce custom MTIA chips through 2029, with an initial commitment exceeding 1 gigawatt in what the companies called “the first phase of a sustained, multi-gigawatt rollout.”

In the same month, [Broadcom and Google locked in a long-term TPU and networking supply agreement running through 2031](https://www.reuters.com/business/broadcom-signs-long-term-deal-develop-googles-custom-ai-chips-2026-04-06/), with Anthropic separately securing access to 3.5 gigawatts of TPU AI capacity from 2027 onward.

Each of these deals is structured as a multi-year supply contract, not a purchase order, and Broadcom has already secured leading-edge wafer capacity, high-bandwidth memory, and substrate commitments through 2028 to back them.

On the Q1 call, Tan delivered the line that reframed the entire investment case: “Today, in fact, we have line of sight to achieve AI revenue from chips, just chips, in excess of $100 billion in 2027.”

Meanwhile, Broadcom’s Q2 FY2026 guidance of approximately $22 billion in revenue (up 47% year-on-year) and $10.7 billion in AI semiconductor revenue (up 140% year-on-year) suggests that ramp is already underway.

Broadcom.overview: Broadcom offers a portfolio of AI accelerators and related software solutions targeting hyperscale cloud providers. Its accelerator business is anchored by six major customers—Google, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and two undisclosed hyperscalers—each with multi‑gigawatt, long‑term contracts. Shipment volumes accelerated in Q3 2026, with a more than 3.5‑fold YoY increase, accounting for 73 % of Broadcom’s AI revenue and featuring custom chips such as Jalapeno for OpenAI and high‑volume Ironwood and TPU v8i parts. Broadcom also markets software subscriptions like VMware Cloud Foundation, priced at $200–$400 per core per year (with a disclosed $350 per core example), supporting the deployment of its AI hardware in data‑center environments.

Intel Corp.overview: Intel's Gaudi family is a line of data‑center AI accelerators designed to run large language models and other deep‑learning workloads. The latest generation, Gaudi 4, is slated for volume production in the second quarter of 2026 after a delay from an originally targeted Q4 2025 launch. Third‑party estimates place the list price of a Gaudi 4 unit at roughly $25,000–$30,000. Intel markets the Gaudi chips to cloud service providers and AI developers in Europe and the United States as part of its AI computing offering.
